aboutPage.p1: ValueVault was born from a very specific need: to stop managing an investment portfolio across a dozen tabs, spreadsheets and scattered apps. Today it's an institutional-grade fundamental analysis platform: automatic DCF with a WACC×growth sensitivity matrix, free cash flow adjusted for stock-based compensation (SBC), maintenance vs. growth CapEx split, and financial health scores (Altman Z, Piotroski F, Beneish M) to catch red flags before you invest. All of it turned into clear charts, heatmaps and gauges — so you can read at a glance what would otherwise be endless tables.
aboutPage.p2: Reliability and accuracy matter to us more than quantity: we only use primary, institutional sources (Alpha Vantage, Financial Modeling Prep, BLS, WSTS, U.S. Treasury), verified and up-to-date — never invented figures or unsupported opinions. We'd rather show less and have it be true than show more and have it be doubtful.
aboutPage.p3: Beyond each asset's own page, ValueVault tracks trends few free tools cover: revenue segmentation by product for each company, the pulse of the semiconductor market (PPI pricing, worldwide WSTS billings and DRAM/NAND memory spot prices), and an institutional filter in the Screener that combines margin of safety, quality and financial soundness at once. We keep expanding it little by little, calmly, prioritizing reliable data and honest tools over flashy ones.

guide.pageSubtitle: A quick guide to the app's sections and tools. Tap each block to expand it: what it is, how to use it, and how to read it. A glossary follows at the end.
guide.footer: 📖 All tools are for analysis and educational purposes; they do not constitute investment advice. Live data comes from Yahoo Finance, CNN, alternative.me, BLS and the New York Fed.

dashboard.title: Dashboard and Portfolio Risk
dashboard.what: Your portfolio valued in euros: total value, size-weighted return, and a quantitative risk block (annualized volatility, max drawdown, and a correlation matrix between positions).
use: Add each asset with its share count and currency so the value and P&L in € are real.
Click "↻ Update prices" to refresh quotes for the whole portfolio.
The "Portfolio Risk" block is only calculated on open (1-year history, Yahoo).
read: "Weighted return (€)" weighs each position by its size — no longer a misleading simple average.
Volatility = how much it swings; Max drawdown = worst decline; low average correlation = good diversification.
"Low risk (perceived)" is your manual label; the MEASURED risk is in the block below.

assets.title: Asset Card (Score · Quality · Consensus)
assets.what: When you expand an asset: Composite Score (Value/Quality/Momentum 0-100), Capital Quality (ROIC vs WACC + FCF yield), EPS Revisions, Analyst Consensus, and process fields (alpha engine, target, stop, catalyst).
use: Click "📊 Fundamentals" to fetch ROIC/FCF/WACC + EPS revisions + consensus (requires login; uses Alpha Vantage quota only when you request it).
Edit the asset to set size, currency, alpha engine, target price, stop, and catalyst.
"🔄 Update market data" refreshes price and basic fundamentals.
read: The Score turns ~24 ratios into 3 decisions. Momentum carries a * if there are no analyst revisions yet.
✓ creates value badge = ROIC > WACC (quality business); ✗ destroys value = ROIC < WACC.
Green EPS Rev. = analysts are raising estimates (fundamental momentum). Consensus: target price and % upside.

watchlist.title: Watchlist
watchlist.what: Your watch list: stocks you're following but don't yet hold, kept separate from the real portfolio.
use: Add them with "+ Watchlist": they don't count toward your portfolio's P&L or concentration.
Each row expands with the same metrics as an asset (Score, fundamentals, chart…).
When you actually buy in, edit it and switch the type to "portfolio".
read: Useful for watching without polluting your real portfolio's performance.
Ideal for waiting on a price or a catalyst before buying.

compare.title: Asset Comparison
compare.what: Pit 2-3 assets against each other, metric by metric, to decide between them.
use: Select the assets to compare.
The table highlights the best value for each metric in green and the worst in red.
read: Ideal for choosing between similar candidates (same sector or strategy).
Look at the whole picture: an asset can win on valuation but lose on quality.

charts.title: Charts · Concentration
charts.what: The REAL composition of your portfolio weighted by value in euros: by asset, sector, strategy, risk and horizon, all in %.
use: Requires your assets to have a size (share count) to weight by value.
Each slice shows its % of the total; the tooltip adds the amount in €.
read: "Concentration by Asset" reveals if you depend too much on one position (warning above 25%).
It's real concentration: a large position weighs more than a small one, not counted by units.

indices.title: Stock Indices
indices.what: The world's main indices in real time (Yahoo Finance): S&P 500, Nasdaq 100/Composite, Dow Jones, Russell 2000, VIX, Euro Stoxx 50, IBEX 35, DAX, CAC 40, FTSE 100, Nikkei 225 and Hang Seng.
use: Choose the period: 1M, 3M, 6M, YTD, 1Y and the longer 3Y, 5Y, 10Y and 20Y.
Click ↻ Update to force fresh data (skips the 10-min cache).
In the comparison chart, use "✓ All / ✗ None" to select indices at once.
read: Cards, grouped by region, show the daily change and the period's return.
The line chart compares the cumulative % return of the indices you have active.

sentiment.title: Market Sentiment
sentiment.what: A thermometer of fear and greed: CNN's Fear & Greed Index (0-100 gauge with its 7 components), the VIX, and crypto Fear & Greed.
use: Watch the central gauge: the needle indicates the zone (Extreme Fear → Extreme Greed).
Check the 7 components to see WHAT is driving sentiment (volatility, breadth, put/call…).
Click ↻ Update for fresh data.
read: It's a CONTRARIAN indicator: extreme fear tends to coincide with market bottoms and extreme greed with tops.
High VIX = nervousness; low = calm. Above 30 signals tension.

trends.title: Sector Trends
trends.what: Relative performance of the S&P's 10 sectors (via SPDR ETFs): heatmap, cumulative chart, and table.
use: Short and long periods (up to 10 years), same as in Indices.
"✓ All / ✗ None" buttons for the line chart.
read: The heatmap reveals sector rotation: which sectors lead and which lag.
Strong defensive sectors (Utilities, Healthcare) = cautious market; strong cyclicals (Tech, Consumer) = risk appetite.

macro.title: Macro Research
macro.what: The engine of institutional allocation: the US Treasury yield curve, 10Y-2Y and 10Y-3M spreads with a recession signal, core inflation (CPI), and the Fed's effective rate. Below, 37 curated sources.
use: Observe the shape of the curve (3M → 30Y) and the spreads.
Inflation cards are compared against the Fed's 2% target.
Click ↻ Update to refresh.
read: An INVERTED curve (10Y-2Y < 0) has historically anticipated a recession 12-18 months out.
Inflation above 2% → the Fed keeps rates high → pressure on equities (especially growth).

marketmap.title: Market Map
marketmap.what: A Finviz-style heatmap: ~44 large-cap stocks grouped by sector, colored by their daily change.
use: Each block is a stock; color runs from red (falling) to green (rising), saturating at ±3%.
Double-click a stock to open its page on Finviz.
Click ↻ to refresh (15-min cache).
read: At a glance you see which sectors are driving the market and which are dragging it down that day.
Widespread green = risk appetite; red concentrated in one sector = a sector-specific problem.

valuation.title: DCF + ROIC Valuation
valuation.what: An intrinsic-value calculator via Discounted Cash Flow (DCF), with a CAPM-based WACC helper and a ROIC vs WACC quality check.
use: Type a ticker and click "Fetch data" to auto-fill FCF, shares, debt, price, beta and ROIC.
Adjust the assumptions: growth, years, terminal growth, and WACC.
Use the CAPM panel (rf + β·ERP) and apply it as WACC with one click. The risk-free rate already comes from the real 10Y.
read: Compare intrinsic value/share with the price: "upside" and "margin of safety" show if it's under/overvalued.
ROIC > WACC (positive spread) = the company CREATES value. ROIC < WACC = a possible value trap.
DCF is very sensitive to assumptions: treat it as a range and always demand a margin of safety.

screener.title: Stock Screener
screener.what: A filter builder that opens external screeners (Finviz, StockAnalysis, Yahoo) with your criteria already applied in the URL.
use: Choose sector, market cap, P/E, P/B, dividend, ROE, country, or a preset strategy.
Click the target screener: it opens in a new tab with the filters set.
Below are complementary links (insiders, 13F, SEC EDGAR…).
read: It's the starting point for DISCOVERING ideas; then analyze them in the asset card or in Valuation.
Preset strategies (Value, Growth, Dividend, Momentum) load typical filter combinations.

volprofile.title: Volume Profile & VWAP
volprofile.what: Where volume has actually traded: POC (price with the most activity), Value Area (70% of volume), and anchored VWAP.
use: Type a ticker, choose a range (3M-2Y) and the VWAP anchor (Start, YTD, High, or Low).
The price chart shows VWAP and the POC/VAH/VAL levels; the horizontal profile marks the current price.
read: POC = magnet and support/resistance. Value Area = the "fair value" zone; outside it, price is in discovery.
Price above the anchored VWAP = buyers in control since that point. The 🟢/🔴/🟡 reading sums it up.

trendfollow.title: Trend Following / CTA
trendfollow.what: A CTA-style trend-following system: long/short/flat signal via moving-average crossover (MA50/200) + Donchian channel + ATR, with volatility-target sizing. Includes a universe of 18 uncorrelated markets.
use: "Ticker" tab: type an asset and choose a range; you'll see the signal, the ATR stop, and the suggested size.
Adjust the "volatility target" to recalculate sizing live.
"Universe" tab: cards by asset class colored by signal; tap one to open it in Ticker.
read: "Flat" (sideways) = stay out; it avoids whipsaws in trendless markets.
Volatility-target sizing equalizes risk across very different assets (an index vs. gold).
It's the OPPOSITE of value investing: it doesn't look at what something's worth, but at what price is doing.

smc.title: Smart Money (FVG / Order Blocks)
smc.what: Detection of Fair Value Gaps and Order Blocks, now with volume validation, a strength score (0-100), breaker blocks, multi-timeframe confluence (daily + weekly), and distance to price.
use: Type a ticker and choose a range. The green/red bands mark the nearest active support/resistance.
In the Order Blocks table, sort by "Date" or "Proximity"; zones within <2% of price are highlighted in gold.
Read the Strength column (⚡ = high volume), the ⇄ breaker tag, and ✦ weekly (confluence with the weekly chart).
read: Zones are areas of INTEREST, not signals. Prioritize the ones with higher Strength, with ⚡ and weekly ✦.
A breaker is a broken Order Block that flips its role (support ↔ resistance).
Use them as context alongside Volume Profile, gamma, and valuation — never in isolation.

gamma.title: Gamma / GEX (Options)
gamma.what: Dealer gamma exposure from the options chain (open interest + implied volatility): net GEX, gamma flip, call/put wall, and two charts (strike profile and gamma curve).
use: Type a liquid US underlying (SPY, QQQ, NVDA…) and choose the expiration.
In the strike profile, the ┄ lines mark spot and flip; the gold border marks the walls.
The gamma curve crosses zero exactly at the gamma flip.
read: GEX > 0 (green) = dealers in long gamma → they dampen movement (less volatility).
GEX < 0 (red) = short gamma → they amplify movement (more unstable).
Call wall = resistance/magnet above; put wall = support below. Below the flip, an unstable regime.
It's an ESTIMATE (dealers' actual positioning isn't public) and covers one expiration.

community.title: Community
community.what: A wall where the community shares investment ideas. Text posts with mentions of stocks ($TICKER) and other users (@handle), likes, comments, public profiles, follow/followers, notifications, and discovery (Trending and user search).
use: The first time, choose your public handle (name + @handle + avatar). Your email is NEVER shown.
Post an idea (max. 500 characters): write $MSFT to link a stock and @handle to mention someone.
Give ❤ likes, 💬 comment, and follow other users. Switch the feed between 🌐 Global, 🔥 Trending, and 👤 Following.
Tap a $TICKER to see all posts mentioning it; use the search box to find users; the 🔔 bell (top) collects your notifications.
read: Anyone can READ the wall without logging in; to post, comment, like, or follow you need to log in.
Trending sorts by recent interaction (likes + comments from the last few days); trending tickers are the most mentioned.
It's conversation between users, not advice: these are personal opinions — always cross-check them against your own analysis.

learning.title: Learning · Notes
learning.what: Your investing notebook (in the "My notes" tab of this same section): notes with a topic, tags, and an optional link to an asset in your portfolio.
use: In "My notes" click "+ Add Note": title, topic, source, content, and tags; optionally link it to an asset.
Filter by topic or search by text, tag, or asset.
You can also add an already-linked note from an asset's card.
read: Linking notes to assets gives you the "why" behind each position when you review the portfolio months later.
Documenting the thesis (and the counter-thesis) reduces confirmation bias.

glossary.def: The price level with the most traded volume. Acts as a magnet and support/resistance.
The range where 70% of volume traded. Outside it, price is in "discovery".
Volume-weighted average price from a reference point. Above it = buyers in control.
A 3-candle inefficiency gap that price tends to fill.
The last opposite candle before an impulsive move; a zone where institutional orders were left.
Discounting future cash flows to estimate a company's intrinsic value.
Weighted average cost of capital; the rate at which future cash flows are discounted.
Return on invested capital. ROIC > WACC means the company creates value.
When the 2-year bond yields more than the 10-year (10Y-2Y spread < 0); historically anticipates recession.
Core inflation (excluding energy and food). The Fed's target is ~2%.
A 0-100 sentiment index. Contrarian: extreme fear ≈ bottoms; extreme greed ≈ tops.
The gap between intrinsic value and price. The bigger it is, the more cushion against estimation errors.
A 0-100 summary across three pillars: Value, Quality, and Momentum. Turns many ratios into 3 decisions.
Free cash flow relative to market cap. Cash is harder to dress up than earnings.
A recent change in analysts' earnings forecasts. Upward = positive fundamental momentum.
How much an asset swings (annualized) and its worst decline from a peak.
Measures whether your positions move together (near 1) or offset each other (negative). Low = better diversification.
Dealers' gamma exposure, in $ per 1% move. Positive stabilizes price; negative amplifies it.
The price where total GEX crosses zero. Above it stability tends to dominate; below it, instability.
The strike with the most call gamma (resistance/magnet) or put gamma (support).
A broken Order Block: price pushed through it and it now acts in the reverse role (support ↔ resistance).
In Community, $MSFT links to the stock's page (posts mentioning it), and @handle links to a user's profile.

memoryPrices.title: 📈 Semiconductor Market Trend
memoryPrices.subtitle: Long-run demand and price (worldwide billings + PPI) plus today's DRAM/NAND/HBM memory spot
memoryPrices.billingsNote: Real monthly global semiconductor industry billings (Americas+Europe+Japan+Asia-Pacific). The most direct demand proxy with the longest free history available.
memoryPrices.ppiNote: Quality-adjusted price index (not the spot price): it structurally trends down due to Moore's Law even during severe shortages — useful for the long-run underlying trend, not the current price spike.
memoryPrices.buildingHistory: Building our own spot history — check back in a few days to see the trend chart.
memoryPrices.sourceNote: Sources: memoryindex.io (daily spot, 24h/30d/YoY), U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (semiconductor PPI), WSTS (worldwide billings). 7d/60d/90d/180d are computed against our own accumulated history (blank until enough days of our own data exist); spot history is accumulated by our own daily cron starting today.
